title.en: The data link layer: how two neighbouring machines stay reliable
title.zh: 数据链路层：相邻两台机器之间怎样可靠

description.en: See that the link layer only handles the hop between two neighbouring machines, and understand what frames, the three services, acknowledgements and retransmission, stop-and-wait and the sliding window each solve.
description.zh: 弄清链路层只管相邻两台机器的一段路，懂得帧、三种服务、确认重传、停等与滑动窗口各自解决什么问题。

name.en: The position and role of the data link layer
name.zh: 数据链路层的位置与作用 (role of the data link layer)

name.en: Packets and frames: encapsulation and decapsulation
name.zh: 分组与帧：封装与解封装 (packets, frames, encapsulation)

name.en: The two dimensions of link services and the three combinations
name.zh: 链路层服务的两个维度与三种组合 (types of link services)

name.en: The three link-layer services and where they are used
name.zh: 三种链路层服务及其应用 (the three services and where they are used)
流量控制与停等协议 (flow control, stop and wait, ARQ)

name.en: Sliding window: go-back-N and selective repeat
name.zh: 滑动窗口：回退 N 与选择重传 (go-back-N, selective repeat)

description.en: Thinking the link layer handles the whole route from laptop to server; it only handles the hop between two neighbouring machines.
description.zh: 以为链路层管的是从笔记本到服务器的整条路；它只管相邻两台机器之间的一段。

description.en: Thinking the same frame is carried all the way to the destination; a frame exists only on one link, and at every router it is opened up and wrapped again.
description.zh: 以为同一个帧会一路送到终点；帧只存在于一段链路上，每经过一台路由器都会拆开再重新封装。

description.en: Confusing the link layer's 'connection' with a transport-layer (TCP) connection.
description.zh: 把链路层的「连接」和传输层 (TCP) 的连接混为一谈。

description.en: Thinking every link should acknowledge every frame; for good wired links and for real-time audio and video it is not worth it.
description.zh: 以为所有链路都应该逐帧确认；质量好的有线链路和实时音视频不值得。

description.en: Thinking that when frames are lost you should just resend faster; speed is not the issue, and only acknowledgements and timeouts tell you which frames did not arrive.
description.zh: 以为丢了就加快重发；速度不是问题，要靠确认和超时才知道哪些没送到。

description.en: Thinking the sliding window just means 'send several frames at once'; it also decides how much is resent after an error and how much the receiver must buffer.
description.zh: 以为滑动窗口只是「一次多发几帧」；它还决定出错后重发多少、接收方要缓存多少。

chapter.en: Which hop the link layer handles

prompt.en: In your dorm you open www.unimelb.edu.au on your laptop. As the first step, the laptop sends a frame over Wi-Fi to the router. After sending, it gets no reply at all. What is the most sensible thing for the laptop to do?
prompt.zh: 你在宿舍用笔记本打开 www.unimelb.edu.au。第一步，笔记本通过 Wi-Fi 把一帧数据发给路由器。发出去以后，没有收到任何回音。笔记本最合理的做法是什么？

label.en: Assume it arrived and send the next frame
label.zh: 当作已经送到了，继续发下一帧

feedback.en: No reply means you do not know. Wireless has plenty of interference and losing frames is common, so this would leave lost frames lost for good.
feedback.zh: 没有回音就是不知道。无线干扰多，丢帧是常事，这样会把丢掉的帧永远丢下。

label.en: Wait a short while, and if there is still no reply, send this frame again
label.zh: 等一小段时间，还没回音就把这一帧再发一遍

label.en: Give up and tell the user the page will not open
label.zh: 放弃，告诉用户网页打不开

feedback.en: Losing one frame does not mean the link is broken. Sending it once more will most likely fix it.
feedback.zh: 丢一帧不等于链路坏了。重发一次，多半就好了。

label.en: Send faster and resend the whole page
label.zh: 把发送速度加快，重发整个页面

feedback.en: Speed cannot solve 'not knowing which frame did not arrive'. Sending too fast may even swamp the other side.
feedback.zh: 速度快解决不了「不知道哪一帧没到」。发得太快还可能淹没对方。

explain.en: This is what Wi-Fi does: every frame must be answered (acknowledged), and if no answer comes, it is resent. This lesson is about working out the 'reply', 'how long to wait' and 'how much to resend'.
explain.zh: 这就是 Wi-Fi 上的做法：每一帧都要有回音 (确认)，等不到就重发。这一课就是把「回音」「等多久」「重发多少」弄清楚。

title.en: The link layer handles only the neighbouring hop
title.zh: 链路层只管相邻的一段

text.en: The physical layer only turns bits into signals and sends them out, without caring whether they are right. On the wire there is noise, interference and attenuation, so bits that reach the other end may be flipped, or even lost.
text.zh: 物理层只管把比特变成信号送出去，不管对错。线上有噪声、干扰、衰减，比特到了对面，可能被翻转，甚至丢掉。

text.en: Above the physical layer, the job of the **data link layer** is to send **frames** reliably and efficiently between two **neighbouring** machines.
text.zh: 在物理层之上，**数据链路层** (data link layer) 的任务是：让 **相邻** 的两台机器之间，可靠、高效地送 **帧** (frame)。

svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='640' height='200' fill='#fbfbf8'/><path d='M65,60 V48 H575 V60' fill='none' stroke='#b4402a' stroke-width='2'/><text x='320' y='38' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#b4402a'>端到端：整条路 (更上面的层关心)</text><g stroke='#222' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><rect x='20' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='65' y='118' stroke='none'>笔记本</text><rect x='190' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='235' y='118' stroke='none'>路由器</text><rect x='360' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='405' y='118' stroke='none'>路由器</text><rect x='530' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='575' y='118' stroke='none'>服务器</text></g><g stroke='#222' stroke-width='3'><line x1='110' y1='112' x2='190' y2='112'/><line x1='280' y1='112' x2='360' y2='112'/><line x1='450' y1='112' x2='530' y2='112'/></g><g font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='150' y='84'>链路 1</text><text x='320' y='84'>链路 2</text><text x='490' y='84'>链路 3</text><text x='320' y='172'>每一段链路各有一个链路层在工作，各管各的</text></g></svg>

alt.en: A laptop reaches a server through two routers, split into three links; the bracket above marks end to end
alt.zh: 笔记本经两台路由器到服务器，分成三段链路；上方括号表示端到端

caption.en: 'Neighbouring' means two machines joined directly by the same stretch of medium.
caption.zh: 「相邻」是同一段介质直接相连的两台机器。

text.en: Between your laptop and the router is one hop (Wi-Fi), and between the router and the next device is another (say, optical fibre). Going all the way from the laptop to the server is called end-to-end, and that is the business of the layers above.
text.zh: 你的笔记本和路由器之间是一段 (Wi-Fi)，路由器和下一台设备之间又是一段 (比如光纤)。从笔记本一路到服务器叫端到端 (end-to-end)，那是更上面几层的事。

text.en: For one hop, the link layer does three things:
text.zh: 对这一段，链路层做三件事：

items.en: Offer the network layer a clearly defined service interface: take the packet the network layer of this machine hands over, and deliver it to the network layer of the neighbouring machine.
items.zh: 给网络层一个定义清楚的服务接口：把这台机器网络层交来的分组，送到相邻那台机器的网络层。

items.en: Deal with transmission errors: what to do when bits are flipped or a frame is lost.
items.zh: 处理传输错误：比特翻转了、帧丢了，怎么办。

items.en: Regulate the flow of data (flow control): a fast sender must not swamp a slow receiver.
items.zh: 调节数据流 (流量控制，flow control)：快的发送方不能把慢的接收方淹没。

title.en: Where the link layer lives: half software, half hardware
title.zh: 链路层住在哪：一半软件，一半硬件

text.en: Inside your laptop, the link layer is split into two halves.
text.zh: 在你的笔记本里，链路层分成两半。

svg.en: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 300' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='640' height='300' fill='#fbfbf8'/><g stroke='#222' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><rect x='60' y='14' width='330' height='186' fill='#fff'/><rect x='150' y='28' width='150' height='30' fill='#fff'/><text x='225' y='49' stroke='none'>Application</text><rect x='90' y='70' width='270' height='122' fill='#f1f1ea'/><rect x='150' y='82' width='150' height='30' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='225' y='103' stroke='none'>Network layer</text><rect x='150' y='124' width='150' height='30' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='225' y='145' stroke='none'>Link (driver)</text><rect x='130' y='186' width='190' height='84' fill='#fff'/><rect x='150' y='194' width='150' height='28' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='225' y='214' stroke='none'>Link (NIC logic)</text><rect x='150' y='232' width='150' height='28' fill='#cfe8cf'/><text x='225' y='252' stroke='none'>PHY (physical)</text></g><g font-size='15' fill='#222'><text x='410' y='36'>Computer</text><text x='410' y='96'>Operating system</text><text x='410' y='145'>Driver: software</text><text x='410' y='230'>NIC: hardware</text><text x='410' y='286'>Cable (medium)</text></g><path d='M225,270 Q225,288 300,288 H400' fill='none' stroke='#222' stroke-width='3'/></svg>
svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 300' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='640' height='300' fill='#fbfbf8'/><g stroke='#222' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><rect x='60' y='14' width='330' height='186' fill='#fff'/><rect x='150' y='28' width='150' height='30' fill='#fff'/><text x='225' y='49' stroke='none'>应用 Application</text><rect x='90' y='70' width='270' height='122' fill='#f1f1ea'/><rect x='150' y='82' width='150' height='30' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='225' y='103' stroke='none'>网络层 Network</text><rect x='150' y='124' width='150' height='30' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='225' y='145' stroke='none'>链路层 (驱动)</text><rect x='130' y='186' width='190' height='84' fill='#fff'/><rect x='150' y='194' width='150' height='28' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='225' y='214' stroke='none'>链路层 (网卡电路)</text><rect x='150' y='232' width='150' height='28' fill='#cfe8cf'/><text x='225' y='252' stroke='none'>物理层 PHY</text></g><g font-size='15' fill='#222'><text x='410' y='36'>计算机</text><text x='410' y='96'>操作系统</text><text x='410' y='145'>驱动程序：软件</text><text x='410' y='230'>网卡 NIC：硬件</text><text x='410' y='286'>线缆 (介质)</text></g><path d='M225,270 Q225,288 300,288 H400' fill='none' stroke='#222' stroke-width='3'/></svg>

alt.en: Inside the computer, the driver in the operating system is the software half of the link layer; the network card holds the link-layer circuitry and the physical-layer PHY, connected to the cable
alt.zh: 计算机里，操作系统中的驱动是链路层的软件部分；网卡里有链路层电路和物理层 PHY，连到线缆

caption.en: The software half of the link layer is in the driver, the hardware half is on the network card, which also carries the physical layer.
caption.zh: 链路层的软件一半在驱动里，硬件一半在网卡上，网卡里还带着物理层。

items.en: **Driver**: software in the operating system. It takes packets from the network layer and decides what to give the card and when.
items.zh: **驱动** (driver)：操作系统里的软件。接网络层交来的分组，决定交给网卡什么、什么时候交。

items.en: **Network card** (Network Interface Card, NIC): hardware. It holds the link-layer circuitry and also the physical layer (PHY), which turns bits into signals on the wire.
items.zh: **网卡** (Network Interface Card, NIC)：硬件。里面有链路层的电路，也有物理层 (PHY)，把比特变成线上的信号。

text.en: The usual split is this: work that must be done on every frame, follows fixed rules and has to keep up with line speed (assembling frames, computing checksums) goes in hardware; anything needing flexible judgement goes in software.
text.zh: 常见的分工是：每一帧都要做、规则固定、又要跟得上线速的活 (拼帧、算校验) 放在硬件里；要灵活判断的放在软件里。

body.en: Lesson 1 explained that an upper layer only 'makes a request' to the layer below and does not care how it is done. The network layer's request to the link layer is a single sentence: hand this packet to the neighbouring machine, whose link layer will hand it to its own network layer.
body.zh: 第 1 课讲过，上层只管向下层「提要求」，不管它怎么做。网络层对链路层的要求只有一句：把这个分组交给相邻的那台机器，对方的链路层再交给对方的网络层。

text.en: When sending, the link layer takes a **packet** from the network layer, puts it in the payload field of a **frame**, adds a header at the front and a trailer at the back, and hands it to the physical layer to send. This is called encapsulation. When receiving, it goes the other way: strip the header and trailer, take out the packet and hand it to the network layer, which is called decapsulation.
text.zh: 发送时，链路层从网络层拿到一个 **分组** (packet)，装进 **帧** (frame) 的载荷字段 (payload field)，前面加帧头 (header)，后面加帧尾 (trailer)，再交给物理层发出去。这叫封装 (encapsulation)。接收时反过来：剥掉头尾，取出分组交给网络层，叫解封装 (decapsulation)。

svg.en: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 235' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><defs><marker id='ar2' markerWidth='10' markerHeight='10' refX='9' refY='3' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z' fill='#222'/></marker></defs><rect width='640' height='235' fill='#fbfbf8'/><g stroke='#222' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><rect x='215' y='16' width='210' height='36' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='320' y='40' stroke='none'>Packet (network layer)</text><rect x='130' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='175' y='117' stroke='none'>Header</text><rect x='220' y='90' width='200' height='44' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='320' y='117' stroke='none'>Payload = packet</text><rect x='420' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='465' y='117' stroke='none'>Trailer</text></g><line x1='320' y1='54' x2='320' y2='88' stroke='#222' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#ar2)'/><g font-size='14' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='175' y='158'>Addr., control</text><text x='320' y='158'>Packet from network layer</text><text x='465' y='158'>Checksum</text></g><g font-size='14' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='320' y='194'>Virtual path: the two link layers seem to swap frames directly</text><text x='320' y='216'>Actual path: every frame goes down to the physical layer to be sent</text></g></svg>
svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 640 235' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><defs><marker id='ar2' markerWidth='10' markerHeight='10' refX='9' refY='3' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z' fill='#222'/></marker></defs><rect width='640' height='235' fill='#fbfbf8'/><g stroke='#222' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><rect x='215' y='16' width='210' height='36' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='320' y='40' stroke='none'>分组 (packet)，网络层的单位</text><rect x='130' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='175' y='117' stroke='none'>帧头</text><rect x='220' y='90' width='200' height='44' fill='#dbe8f6'/><text x='320' y='117' stroke='none'>载荷 = 分组</text><rect x='420' y='90' width='90' height='44' fill='#f4d9a8'/><text x='465' y='117' stroke='none'>帧尾</text></g><line x1='320' y1='54' x2='320' y2='88' stroke='#222' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#ar2)'/><g font-size='14' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='175' y='158'>地址、控制</text><text x='320' y='158'>网络层交下来的分组</text><text x='465' y='158'>校验值</text></g><g font-size='14' text-anchor='middle' fill='#222'><text x='320' y='194'>虚拟路径：两端的链路层像在直接交换帧</text><text x='320' y='216'>实际路径：每一帧都要交给物理层才真正送出</text></g></svg>

alt.en: A packet placed in the payload of a frame, with a header in front (address, control) and a trailer behind (checksum)
alt.zh: 分组放进帧的载荷，前面是帧头 (地址、控制)，后面是帧尾 (校验值)

caption.zh: 帧 = 帧头 + 载荷 + 帧尾。

items.en: The **header** holds addresses and control information: who this frame is for and what kind of frame it is.
items.zh: **帧头** 放地址和控制信息：这一帧给谁、是什么类型的帧。

items.en: The **trailer** holds a checksum: the receiver uses it to check whether any bits went wrong. How it is computed comes in the next lesson.
items.zh: **帧尾** 放校验值：接收方用它检查比特有没有出错。怎么算，下一课讲。

items.en: **A packet is the network layer's unit; a frame is the link layer's unit.** A packet travels the whole route, while a frame lives only on one link.
items.zh: **分组是网络层的单位，帧是链路层的单位。** 分组要走完整条路，帧只活在一段链路上。

text.en: The link layers at the two ends seem to exchange frames directly (the virtual data path), but in fact every frame is handed down to the physical layer and reaches the other end over the cable (the actual data path). This matches the idea of layering: each layer pretends to be talking to the same layer on the other side.
text.zh: 两端的链路层像是在直接交换帧 (虚拟数据路径)，其实每一帧都要往下交给物理层，经过线缆才送到 (实际数据路径)。这和分层的想法一致：每一层都假装在和对面同一层对话。

title.en: How many frames does a packet go into

prompt.en: A packet leaves your laptop, passes through routers R1 and R2, and reaches the server. There are three links in all. How many different frames is this packet put into along the way?
prompt.zh: 一个分组从你的笔记本出发，经过路由器 R1、R2，到达服务器。一共三段链路。这个分组在路上一共被装进了几个不同的帧？

label.en: 1, the same frame is carried all the way to the server
label.zh: 1 个，同一个帧一路送到服务器

feedback.en: A frame lives on only one link. At a router the frame is opened, the packet is taken out, and it is put into a new frame for the next link.
feedback.zh: 帧只活在一段链路上。到了路由器，帧被拆开，取出分组，再装进下一段的新帧。

feedback.en: Frames are counted per link, not per machine. Four machines have only three links between them.
feedback.zh: 帧是按「链路」数的，不是按机器数。四台机器之间只有三段链路。

label.en: 0, the routers only forward bits and do not open frames
label.zh: 0 个，路由器只转发比特，不拆帧

feedback.en: A router needs the information inside the packet to decide where to send it, so it has to open the frame and take the packet out.
feedback.zh: 路由器要看分组里的信息才能决定往哪送，所以必须拆开帧、取出分组。

explain.en: Three links, three frames. The packet stays the same while the frame around it is replaced on every hop. This is exactly what 'the link layer handles only one neighbouring hop' looks like.
explain.zh: 三段链路，三个帧。分组不变，外面的帧每过一段就换一个。这正是「链路层只管相邻一段」的样子。

title.zh: 两个问题，排出三种服务

text.en: When the network layer makes requests of the link layer, there are only two questions to ask:
text.zh: 网络层向链路层提要求时，只有两个问题可问：

items.en: **Set up a connection first?** Connection-oriented: before sending data, the two neighbouring machines agree and set up a connection. Connectionless: send whenever you like, and each frame is independent.
items.zh: **要先建连接吗？** 面向连接 (connection-oriented)：发数据前，相邻两台机器先约好、建一个连接。无连接 (connectionless)：想发就发，每一帧各自独立。

items.en: **Acknowledge?** Acknowledged: after receiving, the receiver replies with an acknowledgement (ack). Unacknowledged: once received, it is just received, with no reply.
items.zh: **要确认吗？** 有确认 (acknowledged)：接收方收到后回一个确认 (acknowledgement，ack)。无确认 (unacknowledged)：收了就收了，不回话。

text.en: An everyday analogy: ordinary mail is done once it goes in the postbox; registered mail needs a signature for each item; a phone call is first connected and agreed, and during the talk the other person keeps saying 'mm-hm' in reply.
text.zh: 类比日常的通信：平信，投进邮筒就完；挂号信，每封都要签收；打电话，先拨通、说好，说话时对方还会「嗯嗯」回应。

text.en: Why is there no 'unacknowledged connection-oriented' service? The point of a connection is that both sides remember frame numbers and order, and need to know which frame the other side received. Without acknowledgements the sender has no way to know, and the connection becomes a mere decoration.
text.zh: 为什么没有「无确认面向连接」？建连接的意义是双方都记着帧的编号和顺序，要知道对方收到了哪一帧。没有确认，发送方无从知道，连接就成了摆设。

body.en: It refers only to the link between two neighbouring machines and is the link layer's own business. A transport-layer connection (such as TCP) is end-to-end and comes later; the two are not the same thing.
body.zh: 只指相邻两台机器之间，是链路层自己的事。传输层的连接 (比如 TCP) 是端到端的，后面才讲，两者不是一回事。

title.en: Where each of the three services is used, and why
title.zh: 三种服务各在哪用，为什么

rows.en: Send independent frames, no acknowledgement. A lost frame is ignored, or left to the upper layer (transport)
rows.zh: 发独立的帧，不确认。丢了不管，或留给上层 (传输层)

rows.en: Ethernet LANs; real-time audio and video
rows.zh: 以太网局域网；实时音视频

rows.en: Wired links make few errors, so the cost of acknowledging every frame is not worth it. A late audio or video frame is already useless, so it is better to drop it than resend
rows.zh: 有线链路错误很少，逐帧确认的开销不划算。音视频迟到的帧已经没用，宁可丢也不重传

rows.en: No connection; every frame is acknowledged individually; a lost or damaged frame is resent
rows.zh: 不建连接，每一帧单独确认；丢了或坏了就重发

rows.en: Wireless has a lot of interference and loses many frames. If it is not fixed at this layer, the upper layers only notice the loss slowly
rows.zh: 无线干扰多、丢帧多，不在这一层补，上层要慢慢才发现丢了

rows.en: Set up a connection first (agree on the rate and message details); frames are numbered, counted and acknowledged, and order is strictly kept; the connection is released when done
rows.zh: 先建连接 (谈好速率和消息细节)；帧要编号、计数、确认，强制保持顺序；用完释放连接

rows.en: Unreliable links, such as satellite channels
rows.zh: 不可靠的链路，如卫星信道

rows.en: High delay and unreliable. Acknowledgements can be lost too, so the same frame may arrive twice and the order may get scrambled, hence the numbering
rows.zh: 延迟大又不可靠。确认也会丢，同一帧可能收到两次，顺序也可能乱，所以要编号

text.en: The three services are not better or worse, only trade-offs: each extra guarantee costs a bit more overhead and waiting. Good links get fewer guarantees, poor links get more.
text.zh: 三种服务没有好坏，只有取舍：多一层保证，就多一点开销和等待。质量好的链路少保证，质量差的链路多保证。

title.en: Pick a service for the link

prompt.en: Which of the following pairings makes the most sense?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一个配对最合理？

label.zh: 视频通话：有确认面向连接

feedback.en: By the time a resent frame arrives, that moment of the picture has already been played, so it is no use. Real-time data would rather drop frames than retransmit them.
feedback.zh: 重传来的帧到的时候，画面早就播过了，没有用。实时数据宁可丢帧，不要重传。

feedback.en: Wireless has a lot of interference and loses many frames. If the link layer does not acknowledge, a loss takes the upper layers a long time to notice, which is too slow.
feedback.zh: 无线干扰多、丢帧多。链路层不确认，丢了要等上层很久才发现，太慢。

label.zh: 质量很好的有线以太网：无确认无连接
卫星链路：无确认无连接

feedback.en: Satellite links have high delay and are unreliable, so they need acknowledgements and numbering to make sure every frame arrives in the right order.
feedback.zh: 卫星链路延迟大又不可靠，需要确认、编号，保证帧都到、顺序对。

explain.en: Wired Ethernet rarely makes errors, so acknowledging every frame is not worth it, and the occasional loss is fixed by an upper layer. The other scenarios each have their reasons: Wi-Fi needs frame-by-frame acknowledgement, and a satellite link needs a connection first and then numbering.
explain.zh: 有线以太网很少出错，每帧都确认不划算，偶尔丢的由上层补。其余场景各有原因：Wi-Fi 要逐帧确认，卫星要先建连接再编号。

text.en: An acknowledgement is just a reply. How do we use it to make a link reliable? The simplest way is called **stop-and-wait**, the simplest form of ARQ (Automatic Repeat reQuest):
text.zh: 确认只是一个回音。怎样用它让链路变可靠？最简单的做法叫 **停等** (stop and wait)，是自动重传请求 (ARQ, Automatic Repeat reQuest) 的最简形式：

items.en: Send a frame and start a timer at the same time.
items.zh: 发一帧，同时启动一个计时器。

items.en: Stop and wait for the receiver's ack.
items.zh: 停下来等接收方的 ack。

items.en: Only when the ack arrives, send the next frame.
If the timer runs out (a timeout) and there is still no ack, send the same frame again.
items.zh: 计时器到了 (超时，timeout) 还没有 ack，就把同一帧再发一遍。

text.en: The receiver acks only good frames. A damaged frame (checksum mismatch) is simply ignored, with no reply at all, leaving it to the sender's timeout to deal with.
text.zh: 接收方只对好帧回 ack。损坏的帧 (校验对不上) 直接忽略，不回任何东西，让发送方的超时去处理。

text.en: How long should the timeout be? Slightly longer than the round-trip time: the frame going out plus the ack coming back. If it is too short, the frame has actually arrived and only the ack is still on its way, but it is treated as lost and resent for nothing.
text.zh: 超时设多久？要比「帧过去再加 ack 回来」的往返时间略长。设短了，帧其实到了，只是 ack 还在路上，就被当成丢了，白白重发。

title.en: When the ack is lost: why frames need sequence numbers
title.zh: ack 丢了：帧为什么要有序号

alt.en: Timeline: frame 0 arrives, but the receiver's ack 0 is lost; the sender times out and resends frame 0, the receiver recognises the repeated sequence number, discards the frame, and sends the ack again
alt.zh: 时间线：帧 0 到达，接收方回的 ack 0 丢了；发送方超时重发帧 0，接收方认出序号重复，丢弃但再发 ack

caption.en: What was lost is the ack; the frame had actually arrived.
caption.zh: 丢的是 ack，帧其实已经到了。

text.en: In the picture, frame 0 did arrive; what was lost is the ack. The sender does not know, and can only resend after the timeout, so the receiver gets the same frame twice.
text.zh: 图里帧 0 其实到了，丢的是 ack。发送方不知道，只能超时重发，于是接收方收到了同一帧两次。

text.en: How does the receiver tell a 'new frame' from a 'repeated frame'? The sender writes a **sequence number** in the frame header. A repeated frame has the same sequence number as last time: throw it away and do not pass it to the network layer again, but do resend the ack, or the sender will wait forever.
text.zh: 接收方怎么分辨「新的一帧」和「重复的一帧」？发送方在帧头里写一个 **序号** (sequence number)。重复的帧序号和上一次相同：丢掉，不再交给网络层，但 ack 要重发，否则发送方会一直等下去。

text.en: For stop-and-wait, a sequence number of just 1 bit (0, 1, 0, 1......) is enough. At any moment only one frame is on the way, so the receiver only has to tell two possibilities apart, 'the frame just received' and 'the next frame', and one bit has exactly two values.
text.zh: 停等的序号只要 1 个比特 (0、1、0、1......) 就够。任一时刻只有一帧在路上，接收方只需要分辨「刚收过的那一帧」和「下一帧」两种可能，一个比特正好两个值。

text.en: This is also the reason 'frames must be numbered' in the connection-oriented service: acknowledgements get lost, frames get repeated, and order gets scrambled.
text.zh: 这也是面向连接服务里「帧要编号」的理由：确认会丢，帧会重复，顺序会乱。

title.en: The cost of stop-and-wait: the line sits idle most of the time
title.zh: 停等的代价：线大部分时间空着

intro.en: A frame is 1000 bits, the link rate is 1 Mbit/s, and the round-trip time is 20 ms (10 ms each way). How much of the line does stop-and-wait use?
intro.zh: 一帧 1000 比特，链路速率 1 Mbit/s，往返时间 20 ms (单程 10 ms)。停等能用上多少线？

why.en: Sending one frame takes 1 ms, the transmission delay M/R from the last lesson.
why.zh: 发完一帧要 1 ms，就是上一课的传输延迟 M/R。

why.en: After sending, we wait for the frame to reach the other end and the ack to come back, one round trip. The ack is tiny, so its sending time is ignored.
why.zh: 发完之后，要等帧到对面、ack 回来，一个往返。ack 很短，它的发送时间忽略。

why.en: Sending a frame and then waiting for its ack is one cycle; the next frame can be sent only when it ends.
why.zh: 发一帧再等 ack，是一个周期；下一帧要等到它结束才能发。

why.en: Out of 21 ms, only 1 ms is actually spent sending data.
why.zh: 21 ms 里只有 1 ms 真的在送数据。

outro.en: On a 1 Mbit/s link, only about 48 kbit/s is actually used. The longer the line (the longer the round trip) and the higher the rate (the faster a frame is sent), the worse the waste. This calculation is not in the slides; it is here to show what is wrong with stop-and-wait.
outro.zh: 1 Mbit/s 的链路，实际只用了约 48 kbit/s。线越长 (往返越久)，速率越高 (发一帧越快)，浪费越严重。这个计算课件里没有，放在这里是为了看清停等的毛病。

prompt.en: A frame is 12000 bits (1500 bytes), the link rate is 10 Mbit/s, and the round-trip time is 4.8 ms. With stop-and-wait, what is the link utilisation (%)?
prompt.zh: 帧长 12000 比特 (1500 字节)，链路速率 10 Mbit/s，往返时间 4.8 ms。用停等协议，链路的利用率是多少 (%)？

hints.en: First work out how long it takes to send one frame: $M/R$.
Utilisation = time to send a frame / (time to send a frame + round-trip time).
hints.zh: 利用率 = 发一帧的时间 ÷ (发一帧的时间 + 往返时间)。

explain.en: Sending a frame takes $12000/(10\times10^6)=1.2$ ms, one cycle is $1.2+4.8=6$ ms, so utilisation is $1.2/6=20\%$.

title.en: Flow control, and getting several frames onto the line at once
title.zh: 流量控制，以及让多帧同时在路上

text.en: **Flow control** solves this problem: the sender is fast and the receiver is slow, so the receiver cannot keep up, its buffer fills, and later frames are dropped. The remedy is hidden in the acknowledgements: if the receiver is not ready, it replies with the ack later, and the sender, getting no ack, does not send the next frame. The pace is left to the receiver. Stop-and-wait carries this function naturally.
text.zh: **流量控制** (flow control) 要解决的问题：发送方快，接收方慢，接收方来不及处理，缓冲区被填满，后来的帧就丢了。办法就藏在确认里：接收方没准备好，就晚点回 ack；发送方收不到 ack，就不发下一帧。节奏交给了接收方。停等天然就带着这个功能。

text.en: But stop-and-wait has just one frame on the way at a time, which is too slow. The fix is direct: do not wait for the ack, send several frames in a row. This is the **sliding window**:
text.zh: 但停等一次只有一帧在路上，太慢。改进的办法很直接：不等 ack，连着发好几帧。这叫 **滑动窗口** (sliding window)：

items.en: Window size W: at most W frames can be sent but not yet acknowledged.
items.zh: 窗口大小 W：已发出、还没收到 ack 的帧，最多能有 W 个。

items.en: Each time an ack arrives, the window slides forward one place, and one more frame can be sent.
items.zh: 每收到一个 ack，窗口就向前滑一格，又可以多发一帧。

items.en: Stop-and-wait is the special case W = 1.
items.zh: 停等是 W = 1 的特例。

text.en: Back to the earlier example with 1000 bits and a 20 ms round trip: with W set to 21, by the time one round of sending is finished the first ack has just arrived, and the line is nearly full. The cost is that sequence numbers must run past the window size (1 bit is no longer enough), and the receiver needs buffer space to hold the frames it receives.
text.zh: 回到前面 1000 比特、往返 20 ms 的例子：W 取 21，发完一轮正好等到第一个 ack，线就接近满了。代价是：序号要比窗口多 (1 个比特不够了)，接收方也要有缓冲来存收到的帧。

body.en: The bigger the window, the more fully the bandwidth is used; but also the more buffer space is needed and the more frames must be resent after an error. Next we look at two ways to handle errors, standing at the two ends of this trade-off.
body.zh: 窗口越大，带宽用得越足；缓冲空间和出错后要重发的帧也越多。接下来看出错时有两种处理，正好站在这个权衡的两端。

title.en: Frame 2 is in error: go-back-N and selective repeat
title.zh: 帧 2 出错：回退 N 与选择重传

text.en: Frames 0 to 5 are sent in a row within the window, and frame 2 is damaged on the way while the others are fine. There are two ways to handle it:
text.zh: 窗口里连发了帧 0 到 5，帧 2 在路上坏了，其余都完好。两种办法：

alt.en: Left: go-back-N, the receiver drops 3, 4, 5 and the sender resends frames 2 to 5, four in all. Right: selective repeat, the receiver buffers 3, 4, 5 and only frame 2 is resent
alt.zh: 左：回退 N，接收方丢弃 3、4、5，发送方重发 2 到 5 共四帧。右：选择重传，接收方缓存 3、4、5，只重发帧 2

caption.en: The same error, two ways of cleaning up.

items.en: **Go-back-N**: the receiver accepts only the frame that is exactly the next one. Frame 2 is damaged, so the later 3, 4, 5 are all dropped. After a timeout the sender resends everything from the damaged frame on: 2, 3, 4, 5. Frames 3, 4, 5 had actually arrived once already, so sending them was wasted.
items.zh: **回退 N** (go-back-N)：接收方只收「正好是下一个」的帧。帧 2 坏了，后来的 3、4、5 都丢掉。发送方超时后，从出错的那一帧起全部重发：2、3、4、5。3、4、5 其实已经到过一次，白发了。

items.en: **Selective repeat**: the receiver stores the good frames that arrive later and sends a Nak (negative acknowledgement) asking for frame 2 alone to be filled in. Once it arrives, frames 2 to 5 are handed to the network layer in order.
items.zh: **选择重传** (selective repeat)：接收方把后到的好帧存起来，发一个 Nak (否定确认，negative acknowledgement) 要求只补帧 2。补到之后，2 到 5 按顺序交给网络层。

rows.en: Resent after one frame is in error
That frame and every frame after it

text.en: This is the trade-off in the sliding window: use the bandwidth effectively, or save buffer space at the data link layer.
text.zh: 这就是滑动窗口里的权衡：有效利用带宽，还是节省数据链路层的缓冲空间。

title.zh: 回退 N 要重发几帧

prompt.en: The sender sends frames 0 to 7, eight in all, in a row in its window. Frame 3 is damaged and the rest arrive normally. With go-back-N, how many frames does the sender have to resend in total?
prompt.zh: 发送方窗口里连发了帧 0 到 7 共八帧。帧 3 损坏，其余都正常到达。用回退 N，发送方一共要重发多少帧？

hints.en: Go-back-N: from the damaged frame on, every frame after it is resent.
hints.zh: 回退 N：从出错那一帧起，后面所有帧都要重发。

explain.en: Everything from frame 3 on is resent: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, five frames in all. With selective repeat, the receiver would store 4 to 7 and only frame 3 would be resent, one frame.
explain.zh: 从帧 3 起全部重发：3、4、5、6、7，共 5 帧。若用选择重传，接收方存下 4 到 7，只重发帧 3，共 1 帧。

prompt.en: (1) An optical fibre link, a Wi-Fi link and a satellite link: which link-layer service suits each? Give a one-sentence reason. (2) Why is stop-and-wait unsuited to long, fast links?
prompt.zh: （1）一条光纤链路、一条 Wi-Fi 链路、一条卫星链路，各适合哪种链路层服务？用一句话说明理由。（2）为什么停等协议不适合长距离的高速链路？

key_points.en: Optical fibre (wired) makes few errors, so unacknowledged connectionless suits it: the cost of acknowledgements is not worth it, and the odd loss is left to the upper layers
key_points.zh: 光纤 (有线) 错误很少，适合无确认无连接，确认的开销不划算，偶尔的丢失留给上层

key_points.en: Wi-Fi has a lot of interference and loses many frames, so acknowledged connectionless suits it: each frame is acknowledged separately and resent if lost
key_points.zh: Wi-Fi 干扰多、丢帧多，适合有确认无连接，每帧单独确认、丢了重发

key_points.en: A satellite link has high delay and is unreliable, so acknowledged connection-oriented suits it: set up a connection first, and number, acknowledge and keep frames in order
key_points.zh: 卫星延迟大又不可靠，适合有确认面向连接，先建连接，帧要编号、确认、保持顺序

key_points.en: Stop-and-wait sends one frame and must wait a whole round trip before the next; on a long, fast link the line is idle most of the time and utilisation is very low
key_points.zh: 停等一次只发一帧，要等一个往返才能发下一帧；链路又长又快时，大部分时间线是空的，利用率很低

model_answer.en: Optical fibre rarely makes errors, so use unacknowledged connectionless: acknowledging every frame is not worth it, and losses are left to the upper layers. Wi-Fi has a lot of interference and loses many frames, so use acknowledged connectionless: acknowledge every frame and resend when there is no reply. A satellite link has high delay and is unreliable, so use acknowledged connection-oriented: set up a connection, number and acknowledge frames, and guarantee no loss, no repeats and no reordering. Stop-and-wait must wait a round trip after every frame; the longer the line, the longer the round trip, and the higher the rate, the faster a frame is sent, so waiting takes up almost all the time and utilisation is very low. That is why long, fast links need a sliding window, which puts several frames on the line at once.
model_answer.zh: 光纤很少出错，用无确认无连接，每帧确认不划算，丢了让上层处理。Wi-Fi 干扰多、丢帧多，用有确认无连接，每帧都确认，没回音就重发。卫星延迟大又不可靠，用有确认面向连接，先建连接、帧编号、确认，保证不丢不重不乱序。停等发一帧就要等一个往返；线越长往返越久、速率越高发一帧越快，等待占了绝大部分时间，利用率很低，所以长距离高速链路要用滑动窗口，让多帧同时在路上。

explain.en: If you can give the reason for each of the three services, and say that the trouble with stop-and-wait is that only one frame is on the way at a time, then you have understood this lesson.
explain.zh: 能说出三种服务各自的理由，以及停等的毛病出在「一次只有一帧在路上」，就说明这一课弄明白了。

text.en: The link layer handles only the hop between two neighbouring machines: it puts the network layer's packets into frames and carries them across this hop reliably, without overloading the receiver.
text.zh: 链路层只管相邻两台机器之间的一段：把网络层的分组装进帧，在这一段可靠、不过载地送过去。

text.en: There are three services, decided by 'set up a connection or not, acknowledge or not'. Good wired lines do not acknowledge; Wi-Fi has a lot of interference and acknowledges frame by frame; satellite is far away and unreliable, so it sets up a connection first and then numbers frames.
text.zh: 服务有三种，由「要不要建连接、要不要确认」决定。有线线路好，不确认；Wi-Fi 干扰多，逐帧确认；卫星又远又不可靠，先建连接再编号。

text.en: Acknowledgements are used in stop-and-wait: send a frame, wait for the ack, resend on timeout, and use the sequence number to recognise repeated frames. It is too slow, hence the sliding window, which puts several frames on the line at once; on an error, go-back-N saves buffer but wastes bandwidth, while selective repeat saves bandwidth but costs buffer.
text.zh: 确认的用法是停等：发一帧，等 ack，超时就重发，序号用来认出重复帧。它太慢，于是有了滑动窗口，让多帧同时在路上；出错时，回退 N 省缓冲、费带宽，选择重传省带宽、费缓冲。

text.en: One question is still unanswered: how does the receiver know where a frame starts and ends, and how does it find out that a bit has been flipped? That is the content of the next lesson.
text.zh: 还剩一个问题没有回答：接收方怎样知道一帧从哪开始到哪结束，又怎样发现某个比特被翻转？这是下一课的内容。
